newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Coast Guard closes parts of Illinois River.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Coast Guard closes parts of Illinois River.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard, issuing restrictions on the Illinois River as a result of high water, closed three areas to navigation on Wednesday, further snagging barge traffic, officials said.

The closed areas were River Mile 127 to 128 (Liverpool, Ill.); River Mile 140 to 144 (Illinois Department of Conservation Banner Marsh area); and River Mile 166 to 182 (North Peoria to Henry, Ill.,), said chief warrant officer Bob Hildebrand at the U.S. Coast Guard Marine Safety Office in St Louis.

"As of early Thursday, we have no idea when the Coast Guard will open up these areas. It will be based on how fast the high water recedes," said Mike Zerbonia, chief maintenance section, Illinois Waterway project with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in Peoria.
At Starved Rock Lock near Utica, Ill., there were 10 tow boats heading upbound and one tow downbound on hold.
"That is the only bottleneck we have right now because of the flood waters in that areas," Hildebrand said.
Heavy rain late last week and during the past 24 hours raised renewed fears of flooding in the central and lower portion of the Illinois River.
The flooding was caused by a combination of heavy rainfall last week and this week running off frozen ground that prevented absorption, officials said.
